desc:
Encoding. A singly linked list is passed to your function as an array holding the node values from head to tail; an empty array is an empty list. You may build real nodes from it first, or work on the array directly. Lists you return are given as arrays of values from head to tail.

Reverse only the part of the list from position left to position right (both inclusive, counting from 1 at the head). The nodes before left and after right stay where they are. Return the values of the resulting list from head to tail.

For nums = [1,2,3,4,5], left = 2, right = 4 the answer is [1,4,3,2,5]. Aim for a single pass over the list that relinks nodes in place.
hints: Reversing the whole list is a loop that flips next pointers. Here you must reconnect the reversed part to the nodes on both sides.
Walk to the node just before position left (use a dummy node so that left = 1 is not special). Call it pre.

Let cur = pre.next. Repeat right - left times: take nxt = cur.next, unlink it with cur.next = nxt.next and insert it right after pre (nxt.next = pre.next; pre.next = nxt). The first node of the segment slides to its end and automatically connects to the rest.
editorial: Put a dummy node before the head and move pre to the node at position left - 1. The node cur = pre.next is the first node of the segment; it will become the last node of the reversed segment. For each of the next right - left nodes, detach the node that follows cur and insert it directly after pre. After every step the front part of the segment is reversed, and cur.next already points to the first node after the segment, so no extra reconnection is needed.

Time is O(n) with a single pass and space is O(1). Alternatives: reverse the segment as a stand-alone list and then fix four pointers (before, segment head, segment tail, after), which is easier to get wrong at the boundaries; or copy the values into an array and reverse a slice, which uses O(n) memory.
